description: We are a team of software developers and networking enthusiasts passionate about technology, space exploration, and innovation. Our skills include programming, web development, networking, system development, and automation. We aim to build creative, practical solutions using NASA's open data. We welcome motivated teammates with skills in UI/UX design, data analysis, data visualization, and software development. Let's explore, innovate, and build something amazing together!
summary: Earth Jukebox accessible web platform that sonifies NASA Scientific Visualization Studio’s annual night-lights imagery (2012–2023, SVS 5313) aligned with Natural Earth country boundaries. By pairing synchronized 4K night-light visual maps with predictable Web Audio sound synthesis, users can explore 258 world territories and compare brightness shifts over time or between countries through pitch alone. Grounded in research by blind astronomer Dr. Wanda Díaz-Merced, Earth Jukebox empowers blind, low-vision, and hearing users through dual-sensory perception and acoustic reference tones while adhering strictly to scientific honesty: rendered RGB brightness is reported as visual map data, not physical satellite radiance, electricity use, or wealth.
details:
1. WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS

Earth Jukebox ("Hear Earth at Night") transforms twelve years (2012 to 2023) of NASA Scientific Visualization Studio night-lights data (SVS 5313) into an interactive, multi-sensory educational platform. Users can explore 258 world territories, examine synchronized 4K NASA night-light frames, and sonify brightness into clean, continuous musical tones:

• Data Integration: We extract area-weighted Rec.709 RGB luma (0 to 255) within each Natural Earth 1:10m country polygon, utilizing 4x4 fractional subpixel sampling and cosine-latitude weighting.

• Sound Mapping: Sound is generated entirely offline using the browser-native Web Audio API (triangle wave oscillator, 10 ms attack, 0.8 s hold, 0.3 s release, routed through a DynamicsCompressorNode). The pitch follows one continuous, mathematically reproducible formula:

frequencyHz = 440 * 2^(brightness / 70)

(where 0 brightness = 440 Hz base, and 70 brightness = 880 Hz, exactly one octave higher).

• User Control: Sound never autoplays. Users trigger tones via single-note playback, multi-year comparisons, 2012-2023 historical sweeps, or reference pitch scales.

2. BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

• Accessibility for Blind and Low-Vision Learners: Visual maps exclude visually impaired students. Grounded in research by blind astrophysicist Dr. Wanda Díaz-Merced, Earth Jukebox proves sound is a powerful data-analysis medium.

• Acoustic Reference Tones: A unique accessibility tool plays Darkest, Median, Brightest, and Selected Country, allowing users to understand global brightness distribution purely by ear.

• 100% Offline Capability: Runs completely standalone with zero external API calls, making it ideal for resource-limited schools and universities with intermittent internet.

• Dual-Sensory Redundancy: Sighted users can inspect visual maps and trends with audio muted; blind users can navigate using screen-reader live regions (aria-live) and audio pitch without needing the screen.

3. CREATIVITY AND ORIGINALITY

Unlike traditional sonification projects that apply arbitrary musical melodies or assign random notes to pixels, Earth Jukebox implements a strictly scientific, mathematically continuous sonification engine where pitch directly reflects verified luma values. It also features interactive multi-country comparisons (such as North Korea versus Palestine, or Iraq versus Belgium) with semitone readouts.

4. FACTORS CONSIDERED AND SCIENTIFIC HONESTY

• Rendered Brightness versus Physical Radiance: We transparently disclose to users that scores measure rendered RGB brightness in the SVS 5313 visualization frames, not physical satellite radiance, electrical grid wattage, population, or wealth.

• Null Handling: 71 tiny territories (under 20 pixel coverage, such as Aruba) remain strictly null, never convert to zero, play no misleading tone, and display: "Too small to measure in this map image — not dark."

• Ice Background Suppression: Greenland and Antarctica carry ice suppression filters (status filtered, pitch null) to prevent snow albedo from falsifying brightness rankings. High-latitude regions carry explicit snow advisories.

• Noise Threshold: Differences smaller than 0.1 or 1% are reported as within video noise rather than real change.

5. TOOLS, LANGUAGES AND FRAMEWORKS

• Frontend Architecture: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Lucide Icons.

• Audio Engine: HTML5 Web Audio API (native browser audio synthesis).

• Cartography: Natural Earth Vector Cartography (Admin 0 Cultural Vectors).

• Verification: 24 automated unit tests, 14 cryptographic SHA-256 data bundle checksums.
